text: The distribution of blood flow to the subendocardial, medium, and subepicardial layers of the left ventricular free wall was studied in anaesthetized dogs under normoxic (A), hypoxic (B) conditions, and under pharmacologically induced (etafenone) coronary vasodilation (C). Regional myocardial blood flow was determined using the particle distribution method. In normoxia, a transmural gradient of flow was observed, with the subendocardial layers receiving a significantly higher flow rate compared with the subepicardial layers. In hypoxia-induced vasodilation, this transmural gradient persisted. However, a marked redistribution of regional flow occurred under pharmacologically induced vasodilation. The transmural gradient decreased. Unlike some findings, these experiments suggest that a considerable vasodilatory capacity exists in all layers of the myocardium and can be utilized by drugs. The differences observed for the intramural distribution pattern of flow under hypoxia and drug-induced vasodilation do not fully support the hypothesis that this pattern reflects corresponding gradients of regional myocardial metabolism.
